subject: Staged APAC onramp & EU data residency — renewal + commit top-up
messages:
From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwoodinference.com>
To: Eleanor Price <eleanor.price@atlascare.health>
Cc: procurement@atlascare.health
Date: Fri, 30 Jun 2028 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Staged APAC onramp & EU data residency — renewal + commit top-up

Hi Eleanor / AtlasCare procurement,

Thanks again for the conversation last week — great to see the traction on the Post-Acute pilot. As AtlasCare approaches the renewal window, I wanted to propose a short amendment that covers two things you asked about: (1) an APAC staged onramp (warm standby / pilot pool) to reduce cold-start risk in APAC, and (2) an EU data residency guarantee with cross-region failover controls.

Headlines: 
- Commitment top-up: +30% reserved capacity on your existing Dedicated pool for 12 months (monthly billing amortized). This gets priority scheduling for APAC staging and a burst allocation during rollout.
- EU residency: contract language to ensure primary data stay in EU-region nodes; encrypted KV replication to APAC is permitted only for failover and is encrypted-in-transit and at-rest.
- Cross-region failover: automated failover policy with RTO target of 90s, and telemetry hooks for you to opt into shorter or longer failover windows.
- Pricing: blended unit price for the top-up; I attached an initial amendment + an APAC SKU matrix so you can see the cost delta by burst level.

Attachments: redwood-commit-amendment-v1.pdf, apac-staging-sku.xlsx

Next steps I propose: 
1) Quick tech deep-dive with Sean to confirm failover design (30–45 min)
2) Procurement and legal review amendments and return redlines
3) Sign amendment and schedule staged capacity deploy (target: mid-July pilot)

Are you available for a technical call Tues 3 Jul morning UK time? If that works I’ll send a calendar invite and include Sean and Marissa.

Thanks,
Ben
Ben Carter
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
ben.carter@redwoodinference.com
+1 (415) 555-0123

---
Note: the PDF here is a draft amendment, not yet legal-signed.

Ben — thanks for the clear summary. A few quick clarifying questions from procurement and infra: 

1) Data residency & replication: when you say "KV replication to APAC" what exactly is replicated? Will customer PII ever be replicated outside EU? We need explicit language that PII is not mirrored.
2) Failover behavior: 90s RTO sounds promising — can you share expected failover latency ranges for typical workloads (LLM chat, embeddings)? We need this for our risk assessment.
3) SOC 2 / evidence: procurement has asked for the most recent SOC 2 report + details of audit scope if not included previously.
4) Pricing: procurement would prefer a quarterly invoicing cadence for the top-up. Is that feasible, or do you need monthly billing?

We can do the tech call on Tue 3 Jul 09:30 BST with Sean. I’ll include our infra lead on that invite (procurement is cc'd).

Eleanor

AtlasCare Health

Thanks Ben — quick notes / redline guidance below. I attached a short redline with the suggested language (redlines_20280630.pdf). Key points: 

- PII carve-out: we can add a clause that PII (as defined in their DPA) is excluded from any cross-region replication. We should reference their DPA definition and require them to identify PII fields during onboarding; operationally we will scope replication to non-PII KV namespaces.
- Failover SLA: 90s RTO is our target for the automatic failover policy; we should add an operational caveat that hot cold-cache performance varies by model and sequence length — include the quantiles (p50/p95/p99) in Sean's tech note rather than in the contract.
- Billing cadence: finance generally prefers monthly for committed pools, but we can offer quarterly invoicing as an exception for enterprise renewals if procurement signs a brief payment amendment. Sean / Finance to confirm collection risk.
- SOC 2: provide the latest SOC 2 Type II report and a summary of scope. Sean, can you confirm what redacted artifacts we can share and attach to the amendment?

Action items for me: I’ll turn the redline into a DocuSign-ready amendment and insert the PII carve-out language. If procurement insists on quarterly billing, we’ll add a payment amendment requiring pre-payment on a quarterly basis.

Marissa
Marissa Cole
